guide.name: Great Smoky Mountains from Cades Cove to Kuwohi
guide.description: Three or four days in the country's most visited national park: a hike-in lodge, waterfall walks, old farm valleys full of deer and elk, and pancakes in the towns at either end.

properties.name: LeConte Lodge
properties.notes: Rustic cabins near the top of Mount Le Conte, reached only on foot. Dinner and breakfast are included, there's no electricity in the rooms, and the sunrise from Myrtle Point is the reason to go. Rooms go fast, so book as early as they allow.

match.skip: Hike-in lodge; Apple Maps only has the Sevierville booking office

properties.name: Buckhorn Inn
properties.notes: A quiet 1938 inn on the Greenbrier side of Gatlinburg, looking straight at Mount Le Conte. Far enough from the Parkway to hear the creek, close enough for an early start.

properties.name: Dancing Bear Lodge
properties.notes: Cabins in the woods in Townsend, the quiet side of the Smokies, about twenty minutes from Cades Cove.
properties.address: 7140 E Lamar Alexander Pkwy, Townsend, TN 37882

properties.name: Fryemont Inn
properties.notes: A 1920s bark-covered lodge above Bryson City, with a big stone fireplace and porch rockers. Handy for Deep Creek and the North Carolina side.

properties.name: Elkmont Campground
properties.notes: The park's biggest campground, along the Little River near the old Elkmont summer cabins. In early June it's the heart of the synchronous firefly season. Viewing is by lottery, so check the park site.

properties.name: Cades Cove Campground
properties.notes: Camp at the mouth of the cove and you can be on the loop road at first light, before the cars, when the deer and bears are out.

properties.name: The Pancake Pantry
properties.notes: Gatlinburg's pancake house since 1960. There's usually a line, and it moves. Go early on a hiking day.

properties.name: Wild Plum Tea Room
properties.notes: Lunch in a little cabin in the woods off the Arts and Crafts loop. Save room for dessert.

properties.name: The Greenbrier Restaurant
properties.notes: Steaks and trout in an old log lodge up the hill from Gatlinburg. The dinner to book after a long hike.

properties.name: Peter's Pancakes & Waffles
properties.notes: A big breakfast by the Oconaluftee River in Cherokee before you drive up Newfound Gap Road.

properties.name: Nantahala Brewing
properties.notes: Bryson City's own brewery, full of muddy boots and paddlers at the end of the day.

properties.name: Sugarlands Visitor Center
properties.notes: Start here on the Tennessee side for maps, ranger advice and the day's road closures. You need a parking tag to park anywhere in the park for more than a few minutes, and they sell them here.
properties.address: 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Rd, Gatlinburg, TN 37738

properties.name: Oconaluftee Visitor Center
properties.notes: The North Carolina side's visitor center, next to the Mountain Farm Museum's log buildings. Elk often graze the fields here at dusk.

properties.name: Cades Cove
properties.notes: An eleven-mile one-way loop through an old farming valley, past log churches, cabins and Cable Mill. Go at sunrise for deer and bears, and check the park site for car-free mornings, when it's all bikes.
properties.address: Cades Cove Loop Rd, Townsend, TN 37882

properties.name: Kuwohi
properties.notes: The highest point in the park, once called Clingmans Dome, renamed with its Cherokee name in 2024. A steep paved half mile leads to the observation tower. The road closes in winter.
properties.address: Clingmans Dome Rd, Bryson City, NC 28713

properties.name: Newfound Gap
properties.notes: The pass on the state line, where the Appalachian Trail crosses the road and Roosevelt dedicated the park in 1940. Cold and windy most of the year, so bring a layer.

properties.name: Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail
properties.notes: A slow, narrow one-way drive past old homesteads, mossy boulders and the Place of a Thousand Drips after rain. Closed in winter.
properties.address: Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail, Gatlinburg, TN 37738

properties.name: Mingus Mill
properties.notes: An 1886 mill that still grinds corn with a water turbine. A five-minute stop just up the road from Oconaluftee.

properties.name: Cataloochee Valley
properties.notes: A remote valley at the end of a winding gravel road, with old frame houses and the park's best elk watching at dawn and dusk. Worth the detour, and far quieter than Cades Cove.

properties.name: Museum of the Cherokee People
properties.notes: The story of the Cherokee in these mountains, told by the Eastern Band, from long before the park to the Trail of Tears and today.

properties.name: Great Smoky Mountains Heritage Center
properties.notes: Mountain life before the park, with moved-in cabins and farm buildings out back. A good rainy-morning stop on the way to Cades Cove.

properties.name: Alum Cave Trailhead
properties.notes: The classic Smokies hike: Arch Rock, Inspiration Point and the Alum Cave Bluffs, about five miles round trip. Keep going to LeConte Lodge if you've booked a night. The lot fills by mid-morning.

properties.name: Chimney Tops Trailhead
properties.notes: A short, steep climb to a viewpoint facing the Chimney Tops. The rock summit has been closed since the 2016 fire, and the view from the end of the trail is still the reward.

properties.name: Grotto Falls
properties.notes: An easy walk through old hemlock forest to the one waterfall in the park you can walk behind. Start from the Trillium Gap trailhead on Roaring Fork.
properties.address: Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail, Gatlinburg, TN 37738

properties.name: Abrams Falls Trailhead
properties.notes: Five miles round trip along Abrams Creek to a short, wide waterfall and a deep pool. Pair it with the Cades Cove loop. Don't swim near the falls, where the current is strong.
properties.address: Cades Cove Loop Rd, Townsend, TN 37882

properties.name: Andrews Bald
properties.notes: A grassy mountaintop meadow with flame azaleas in June, down the Forney Ridge Trail from the Kuwohi parking area. Easy going down, a real climb coming back.
properties.address: Clingmans Dome Rd, Bryson City, NC 28713

properties.name: Charlies Bunion
properties.notes: A rocky knob with a huge view, about eight miles round trip on the Appalachian Trail from Newfound Gap. Start early, as the gap's lot fills fast.

properties.name: Porters Creek Trail
properties.notes: The spring wildflower walk, along a creek past an old farm site and a cantilevered barn in the quiet Greenbrier corner of the park.

properties.name: Deep Creek Trailhead
properties.notes: Three waterfalls on an easy loop a few minutes from Bryson City. In summer the creek is full of people on inner tubes, rented at the outfitters by the entrance.
properties.address: Deep Creek Rd, Bryson City, NC 28713
